name: 27445-varlenlora-gptoss120b-1gpu
model: openai/gpt-oss-120b, served with one LoRA adapter attached (LevinZheng/gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter, addressed as `lora1`)
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one vLLM engine.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1, no warmup and no cooldown, bounded at 40 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, static seed 27445.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, prompt length drawn per request in [1520, 1680] tokens and output length in [190, 210], both uniform, output enforced with EOS ignored, temperature 0.
purpose: A specialist-tuned 120B assistant drafting short replies from long briefs, one user at a time, single GPU.
launch:
model: openai/gpt-oss-120b

tensor-parallel-size: 1

trust-remote-code: true

# `max-lora-rank` is not the adapter's own rank (8); it sizes the per-layer adapter buffers.
# 64 costs ~10.2 GiB here and does NOT fit on one H100: 61 GiB of mxfp4 weights + 10.2 leaves
# ~4 GiB of the 75.6 GiB that 0.95 util gives, and the engine then dies in a restart loop on
# `No available memory for the cache blocks` (measured 2026-08-22, 27 engine starts, every one
# of them that error). 8 costs ~1.3 GiB, leaves ~13 GiB for activations + KV, and is the
# adapter's real rank. The source benchmarked this on 4xB200, not on one H100.
enable-lora: true
max-loras: 1
max-lora-rank: 8

max-num-seqs: 8

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.95

enable-prefix-caching: false

max-model-len: 4096
